Context.lead: Four sources land in Snowflake once a day; dbt models build the vehicle view; three consumer groups read it.

subsections.title: Snowflake and Airflow in this flow

items: Snowflake holds raw, core and marts; retention is a table property, so the seven-year cost history (FLT-7) lives in `core` tables, not in Time Travel.
Airflow runs one DAG at 05:00: three extracts, COPY INTO raw, dbt build, dbt test, dashboard refresh by 07:00 (FLT-2).
The fuel statement has no connector; finance uploads it to a Snowflake stage once a month until the provider offers SFTP or an API.

Requirements.lead: 12 items from the epic. Status: clear = buildable as written · gap = information missing · conflict = two requirements disagree.

subsections.title: FLT-4 vs FLT-2, FLT-7 vs the telematics contract

items: FLT-4 vs FLT-2: the daily batch cannot alert within an hour. MVP alerts next morning from the batch; the hourly path is phase 2 (section 9, Alerts).
FLT-7 vs telematics contract: we keep our own `core` tables for seven years; raw telematics older than 24 months is not re-fetchable. Owner to decide: archive raw files too.

Identity and linking.lead: The vehicle is the one entity everything hangs on; VIN is the master key, plate and fuel card are mapped to it with validity dates.

subsections.title: VIN as master key; plate and card mapped by date

items: Master key is `vin`; `vehicle_id` is kept as the FMS surrogate.
Plate → VIN: a mapping table with `valid_from`/`valid_to`, built from the daily FMS snapshots, so a work order joins the vehicle that carried the plate on `opened_at`.
Card → VIN: same pattern on `card_no`; FMS holds today's assignment only, so re-assigned cards before the first snapshot cannot be attributed. Owner to decide: accept, or ask FMS for history.
Telematics VINs unknown to FMS are loaded and reported, not dropped (section 8: 3 of 20 VINs).

Data findings.lead: Two sample files profiled, structure only: FMS vehicles (20 rows) and three days of telematics (60 rows). Values of sensitive-looking columns are withheld.

subsections.title: VIN overlap, empty cards, empty odometers

items: 17 of 20 FMS VINs appear in telematics; 3 telematics VINs are unknown to FMS: likely decommissioned or wrongly keyed vehicles. We load and report them (section 5).
`card_no` is empty for 25% of vehicles: fuel cost cannot be attributed for a quarter of the fleet until FMS is completed.
`odometer_km` is empty in 5% of readings: the FLT-12 rule compares against the last non-empty reading.
`fault_code` is set in 22% of readings; severity is always set with it.
`plate` is unique in the sample, which supports the plate mapping; its stability over time is not visible in three days.

items: Manual fuel upload is skipped in a month: cost per vehicle is understated. Mitigation: a freshness test on `raw.fuel_txn` alerts finance.
Plate re-registration between two snapshots goes unseen: a work order joins the wrong vehicle. Mitigation: unknown-plate report after each run.
Telematics VINs unknown to FMS grow over time: fleet counts drift between dashboard and FMS. Mitigation: the unknown-VIN report is reviewed weekly by the fleet manager.
